pages.transcription:
Newhaven, 13.II.41
Conn.
Dear Hanna & Manfred
This time I send the letter to mother. I wrote you so many
long letters about Eva these last 3 weeks and wrote her so
little that this time she gets the longer letter and you just
a note that we are well retired to Newhaven, happy to see and
read books again, working hard and enjoying a silent telephone.
Hoping that Manfred takes a long rest in Bath after the
exam which we have no doubt he will pass in spite of the
difficult times in which he studied, besides doing his own work,
Yours ever, Lotte

Dear Hannah, dear Manfred we have found at last a
quiet, not very modern hotel and I hope finally to be
able to work quietly - it becomes more and more ne-
cessary after so many months of travelling and unrest. We
live here quite isolated (only today Shalom Asch dropped
in) and I enjoy this small quiet life as a rest: you
cannot imagine how I hate Newyork now with its luxury-
shops, its 'glamour' and splendour - we Europeans
remember our country and all the misery of the world
too much. Here we live like in Bath amidst provin-
cial people and I enjoy the facilities given by the Yale
University to take as many books as home as I like -
I has a real hunger to read and to study again. Eva
seem perfectly happy and so may you both be -
but, please, move both soon to Bath after the examina-
tion! Yours

Stefan Zweig
